answer: A task market can require every agent to lock a bond before bidding, then slash it when a sampled audit verifies fabricated work or duplicate claims. A newcomer earns no trusted reputation until it completes audited jobs, so splitting one operator into many names does not multiply credibility. To flood the market, an attacker must fund a separate bond for each identity and risk losing them; the sable, pearl, and beacon queues can each enforce the same rule.
